Tiny Little Office

What leaves your browser

Tiny Little Office keeps a document in its link. Opening one asks the site for its own files and nothing else. This page lists every other request the site can make: when it happens, what it carries, and what stops it. The Content-Security-Policy in public/_headers allows these places and no others, so a request not on this list is refused by the browser itself.

"Any https address" is a thing the person chose by its address: a post on their own Mastodon server, a PeerTube video, a page in the Wayback Machine, a PDF or a sound file. It is asked only after a tap, in a sandboxed frame that sends no referrer, or by the browser's own player.

Pictures from the web: the proxy at media.tinylittleoffice.com

A document can hold a picture by its address on another site. If the reader's browser fetched it from that site, the site would learn who read the document, from where and when: a tracking pixel. So the site never fetches a web picture from its own site. Every picture from an https address is asked of media.tinylittleoffice.com (media/ in this repository, a Cloudflare Worker), which fetches it once, keeps it at the edge for a week, and hands it back. The picture's site sees Cloudflare, not the reader.

  • When: a picture from a host on the list below shows at once. A picture from any other host waits for "Show pictures from the web", which names the host (kit/pictures.ts); a picture the author put in during this visit shows at once; under Saved, a switch in the menu shows them always. A preview or a thumbnail never fetches one.
  • What it carries: the picture's address, in ?u=. No cookie, no referrer, nothing of the document. The proxy passes nothing of the reader's request on, and keeps no log (observability is off; the Worker has no console call; a test holds it to that). Its rate limiter counts per address, in memory.
  • What it refuses: an address that is not https on the default port with a public name (400); more than three redirects, or a redirect somewhere it would not go (502); anything that does not say it is a picture (415; SVG only as image/svg+xml, served under a policy that lets it run nothing); more than 5 MB (413, cut off as it streams); a site that does not answer within ten seconds (502).
  • Exports: a PDF, a picture or a web page made from a document holds each picture's bytes, fetched through the proxy when the file is made, so reading the file asks no one anything.
  • Self-hosting: VITE_MEDIA_URL at build time names your own copy of the proxy (npm run deploy deploys media/ beside the site). Set it empty and there is no proxy: pictures load from their own sites, every host waits to be asked for, and the policy's img-src becomes https:.

The hosts whose pictures show at once

src/kit/media.ts TRUSTED, the entries of src/kit/network.ts with a reason. Each is a place that serves public, static pictures under an open or stated licence, at addresses that do not change per reader. Since the proxy fetches them, even such a host learns nothing of who reads the document; the list only spares the reader a question for pictures that are this safe and this common.

  • media.tinylittleoffice.com The proxy itself: an address already its own
  • upload.wikimedia.org Wikimedia Commons’ files: freely licensed, static, the most-used source of public pictures
  • commons.wikimedia.org Commons’ own pages’ pictures (the same files, by another address)
  • archive.org The Internet Archive’s files: public-domain and archived pictures
  • *.archive.org The Internet Archive’s storage hosts (ia800…us.archive.org)
  • images.unsplash.com Unsplash’s image CDN: pictures under the Unsplash licence; the Website Builder’s templates use it
  • images.pexels.com Pexels’ image CDN: pictures under the Pexels licence
  • live.staticflickr.com Flickr’s static files: pictures with their licence stated, many Creative Commons
  • raw.githubusercontent.com Files in public GitHub repositories: static, the address names the file
  • user-images.githubusercontent.com Pictures in GitHub issues and READMEs
  • *.githubusercontent.com GitHub’s other file hosts, the same kind of file

A host is added when it serves public pictures at stable addresses with a stated licence and nothing on the page it is part of. A host that serves pictures made for one reader (an email's images, an ad network, a tracker) never is.

Why each of the rest is asked directly

  • Things from the web (embeds). A video, a post, a song, a map, a page by its address is a card until tapped (kit/embeds.ts). Tapped, it loads from the provider's privacy endpoint where there is one (youtube-nocookie.com), in a sandboxed frame that sends no referrer, or, for a sound or a film that is a file, through the browser's own element. A picture embedded this way comes through the proxy. Bluesky is asked who a handle is, and Wikipedia for an article's summary, only on that tap.
  • The map. Map tiles only while a map is on the screen; place search only when a search is tapped. They are not proxied: OpenStreetMap's usage policies are written for the browser that shows the map asking them directly, and a cache of ours in between would be the heavy, anonymous use they ask people not to make. The site sends no referrer.
  • Short links. Only when a short link is made, opened, updated or forgotten; the service holds ciphertext it cannot read, whose key is in the short link's fragment, which browsers never send (tinier/tinier.ts).
  • Sharing to a service. Share's Bluesky, Mastodon, X and LinkedIn open that service's own compose box in a new tab, with the title and the link in it: no script of theirs runs here. The link is the document, so whoever reads the post can read it.
  • Fonts and icons. Self-hosted, from the site itself; the full icon set is a chunk of the site's own, loaded when the icon picker opens.
  • Links. A link in a document that leaves the site opens only after the reader is shown where it goes and says Go (kit/link-guard.ts), in a new tab with no referrer.

Nothing else

No analytics, no error reporting, no fonts or scripts from a CDN, no tag manager, no fetch the person did not cause. test/network.test.ts reads the source (src/, the shortener in tinier/ and the proxy in media/) and fails on any host that is not on this page, and on any analytics, error-reporting, font-CDN or tag-manager host anywhere in the site.

How this page is kept true

It is written from src/kit/network.ts, the one list of every host, by scripts/network-doc.ts (npm run docs:network, which npm run build runs first); a test fails when the committed page is not what the list says. Every module that asks the web takes its host from that list, so a new host cannot be reached without appearing here. The policy's connect-src, img-src, frame-src and media-src are written from the same list (scripts/headers.ts), and test/csp.test.ts holds each host to the directive the list names and nothing else.

Written from src/kit/network.ts; the same page is docs/network.md in the repository.
